questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Deploying the Application”?
options: Deploying the Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Deploying the Application means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Deploying the Application removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Deploying the Application should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Deploying the Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Deploying the Application is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Creating a production build” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Creating a production build” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Creating a production build” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Creating a production build” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Creating a production build” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Creating a production build” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Creating a production build” under Deploying the Application. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Deploying the Application”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
